description: Runs two keywords in one storefront and reports how much their ranked results overlap. Use this BEFORE concluding anything from a rank difference between two queries: rank is relative to whoever else is in that result set, so an app at #19 for one phrase and #131 for another has not necessarily been hurt by the extra word -- the two searches may simply have different competitors. identicalResults: true means Apple answered one query for both (it does this for some accented/unaccented pairs, and for some rewordings), so any rank difference is noise; NULL means both queries returned nothing, so there was no list to compare and no conclusion to draw either way. A low overlap means the two are genuinely different searches and their ranks are not comparable at all.

app.description: Optional app (id, URL, or name) to also report the rank of in each result set, so you can see the rank difference and the overlap that qualifies it together.

b.description: Second search keyword, the one to compare against.

country.description: Two-letter App Store storefront country code, e.g. "us". Defaults to the server's configured default country.

top.description: How deep to compare the two ranked lists (default 25). identicalResults always compares the FULL lists, not just this depth.

name: compare_queries
title: Compare two searches' result sets
